steps.u: Our Terraform plan for the staging VPC wants to recreate the NAT gateway every time. Make it stop.

steps.r:
# aws_nat_gateway.main must be replaced
  ~ allocation_id = "eipalloc-0a1b" -> (known after apply) # forces replacement

steps.a: The elastic IP is being replaced each plan, so the gateway that depends on it is replaced too. Check why the EIP changes.

steps.r: # aws_eip.nat will be updated in-place... tags_all changes (default_tags provider block)

add default_tags to providers
bump aws provider to 5.70

steps.a: The recent provider bump changed how tags_all is computed. That alone should be in-place, not a replacement; the forced replacement comes from allocation_id being 'known after apply' because the EIP resource is flagged as changing. I'll ignore the tag drift on the EIP.

steps.r: No changes. Your infrastructure matches the configuration.

reference.summary: Stopped Terraform from recreating the staging NAT gateway on every plan. The elastic IP showed perpetual tag drift after a provider bump, which marked the gateway's allocation id as changing; ignoring tags_all on the EIP made the plan clean (no changes). Applied to staging config only.
facts: plan replaced the NAT gateway every time
elastic IP showed tags_all changes after the provider bump
added ignore_changes for tags_all on the EIP

decisions.choice: ignore tags_all on the elastic IP instead of removing default_tags
decisions.reason: the default tags are wanted everywhere else, and only this resource's drift forced the replacement
